reference.assembly: S. cerevisiae R64-1-1 (Ensembl iGenomes, as documented by nf-core)
reference.note: Copy upstream reference/genome.fa unchanged. Nuclear chromosome I includes annotated introns.

origin.junction_source: Consecutive exon features grouped by transcript_id and strand, on contig I of the pinned nf-core reference/genes.gtf. These are existing source annotations, not inferred from our aligner results.
origin.source_selection_bam: nf-core WT_REP1.sorted.bam produced by STAR 2.7.11b. It also contains SRR6357071; selection explicitly restricts names to SRR6357070.
origin.transformation: From source BAM, retain complete primary SRR6357070 pairs on I with NH:i:1 for both mates. Divide by whether an N operation matches an annotated intron. Take first 128 names lexicographically in each group. Copy their original untrimmed FASTQ records unchanged from the two pinned nf-core files, in source order. The BAM is used only to choose read names, not to reconstruct sequences or qualities.
limitations: Upstream nf-core enriched reads for chromosome I using Kraken2, then sampled 50,000 pairs with seqtk seed 100; its full procedure is preserved in provenance/nfcore-rnaseq-README.md.
Our further selection enriches for annotated splice-junction reads. It cannot measure splice-junction sensitivity or whole-genome specificity.

Upstream selection BAM contains trimmed reads and some very long apparent introns; our positive splice group requires a junction matching the source exon annotation. Distributed FASTQ reads remain the untrimmed original nf-core records.
No variant, junction or transcript truth set is supplied.

note: This new Cutadapt selection uses the two raw nf-core FASTQ sources directly, not the previous alignment/splice-based fixture selection. Its raw records are unchanged.
